mainTopic: Shoes and leather on שבת; moving a shoe on its last; the new פרק on carrying a child with מוקצה items
overview: The amud opens with how to scrape a dirty shoe on שבת. רבי אבהו says to use the back of a knife, but an elder rejects this from a ברייתא of רבי חייא that forbids all scraping and gives rules about oil and leather. רב חסדא's comment on rolling on a leather mat is reworded to depend on the amount of oil: enough to polish is allowed, enough to tan is forbidden. A ברייתא then lists shoes one may not wear outside on שבת because they may come off and be carried: a shoe too big for a child, a woman's torn shoe, and a woman's new shoe. בר קפרא adds that the new shoe is allowed if she wore it on ערב שבת. Two ברייתות disagree about sliding a shoe off a shoemaker's last. The גמרא explains this as a dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, and tests it against the views of אביי and רבא on moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. After the הדרן for פרק תולין, a new משנה allows lifting a child holding a stone and moving מוקצה together with permitted items. The גמרא examines רבא's ruling about carrying a child with a purse, using the principles חי נושא את עצמו and מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. It ends by starting a challenge to the answer of the school of רבי ינאי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How may one scrape the shoe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what tool one may use to scrape a dirty shoe on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does one scrape it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the earlier discussion, which allowed scraping dirt off a shoe. Now it asks how exactly this should be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scraping is already allowed; the question is only about the method. The concern is that scraping the normal way might look like a forbidden מלאכה, such as smoothing or working the leather.

keyTerms.meaning: With what?
He scrapes it

phrases.english: With what does one scrape it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the dirty shoe from the earlier discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by following up on the earlier permission to scrape a shoe.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The permitted tool or method for scraping a shoe on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: with the back of a knife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that one scrapes with the back (blunt side) of a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: With the back of a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question: use the blunt back of a knife, not the sharp edge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the back of the knife is an unusual way of scraping, a שינוי. This makes it less like real work on the leather, so he allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Back (the blunt side)
Knife
Doing something in an unusual way

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
With the back of a knife.
phrases.notes: The blunt side, not the cutting edge. This is an unusual way to scrape.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Scrape with the back of a knife, in an unusual manner.

steps.title: An elder rejects this: רבי חייא forbids all scraping
steps.stepSummary: An elder tells רבי אבהו to drop his teaching, because רבי חייא's ברייתא forbids scraping any shoe, new or old.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: Remove your teaching in the face of what רבי חייא taught: One may not scrape either a new shoe or an old shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: An elder attacks רבי אבהו's answer. He quotes a ברייתא that says no scraping is allowed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו assumed scraping is allowed and only discussed the method. רבי חייא's ברייתא says scraping is forbidden for every shoe, so there is no method to discuss. The elder tells him to 'erase' his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder
Remove (erase) your teaching
In the face of, because of
Taught (introduces a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: 'סמי' here does not mean 'blind'. It means 'remove' or 'cross out', the way one would delete a mistaken text.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
Remove your [teaching] in the face of
phrases.notes: Your teaching cannot stand against the source I am about to quote.

phrases.english: that which Rabbi Chiya taught:
One may not scrape, neither a new shoe
nor an old shoe,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא: סְמִי דִּידָךְ מִקַּמֵּי הָא דְתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's answer from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's permission to scrape with the back of a knife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids scraping any shoe, so there is no permitted way to do it.

steps.title: Rest of the ברייתא: rules about oil and leather
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. One may not oil a foot that is already inside a shoe. One may oil the foot and then put it in the shoe, and one may oil the whole body and roll on a leather mat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not smear oil on his foot while it is inside a shoe or sandal. But he may smear oil on his foot and then place it into a shoe or sandal. And he may smear oil on his whole body and roll on a leather mat, and he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still the quote from רבי חייא's ברייתא. It adds rules about oil soaking into leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oiling a foot inside the shoe works oil straight into the leather, which looks like עיבוד (tanning), so it is forbidden. Oiling first and then putting the foot in is the normal way of oiling oneself and is allowed. The same applies to rolling on a leather mat after oiling the body: any effect on the leather is incidental.

keyTerms.meaning: He may smear (oil)
Sandal
Rolls around
A leather mat or rug
He need not worry
Tanning leather, a forbidden מלאכה

steps.whyThisMatters: The last clause, about rolling on a leather mat, is the clause that רב חסדא comments on in the next step.

phrases.english: And one may not smear his foot with oil
while it is inside the shoe
phrases.notes: The oil would soak straight into the leather.

phrases.english: or inside the sandal.
But he may smear his foot with oil,
and place it inside the shoe
or inside the sandal.
And he may smear his whole body with oil,
and roll on top of a leather mat,
and he need not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יָסוּךְ אֶת רַגְלוֹ שֶׁמֶן וְהוּא בְּתוֹךְ הַמִּנְעָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not oil a foot while it is inside leather footwear. Oiling first and then wearing the shoe is allowed, and so is rolling on a leather mat after oiling the body.

steps.title: רב חסדא: allowed only for polishing, not tanning
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the leather-mat permission: it applies to polishing, but not to tanning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They only taught this for polishing it, but for tanning it, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a limit to the last ruling of the ברייתא, rolling on the leather mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He separates two purposes. Making the leather shine is allowed. Treating the leather to tan it is forbidden. The next step questions what this distinction really means.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught [this] for
To polish it (make it shine)
To tan it

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They only taught [this] for polishing it,
phrases.notes: This refers to rolling on the leather mat.

phrases.english: but for tanning it, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְצַחְצְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places a limit on the final clause of the ברייתא in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rolling an oiled body on a leather mat is allowed for polishing but forbidden for tanning.

steps.title: Challenging רב חסדא's distinction from both sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: forbidding tanning is obvious, and is anyone really allowed to polish deliberately on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: For tanning it, isn't that obvious? And furthermore, for polishing it, is there anyone who permits that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's statement on both sides. This sets up a new reading of his words, which the next step gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, tanning is a forbidden מלאכה, so there was no need to say it is forbidden. Second, deliberately polishing leather on שבת is also not allowed, so 'polishing is permitted' cannot be right. רב חסדא's words must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
And furthermore
Is there anyone who permits?

steps.confusionAlert: This is a two-part challenge. Both halves of רב חסדא's distinction are attacked, not just one.

phrases.english: For tanning it, isn't that obvious?
phrases.notes: Tanning is a forbidden מלאכה, so why say it?

phrases.english: And furthermore, for polishing it,
is there anyone who permits [that]?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעַבְּדוֹ, פְּשִׁיטָא? וְתוּ: לְצַחְצְחוֹ, מִי אִיכָּא מַאן דְּשָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's distinction from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's split between polishing (allowed) and tanning (forbidden).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying tanning is forbidden is pointless, since it is obvious. Saying deliberate polishing is allowed is wrong, since nobody permits it. So the distinction as stated cannot stand.

steps.title: רב חסדא's statement is reworded: it depends on how much oil is used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא withdraws the earlier version of רב חסדא's statement. It replaces it with a version based on the amount of oil: enough to polish is allowed, enough to tan is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, this is how it was said: רב חסדא said: The permission was only taught when one uses an amount of oil that is only enough to shine the leather. But an amount that is enough to tan the leather is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6 by saying רב חסדא's words were reported wrongly, and it gives the correct version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old version, the difference was what the person was trying to do (polish or tan). That made the rule seem either obvious or strange. In the new version, the difference is the amount of oil. If a person uses enough oil to actually tan the leather, it is forbidden even if he did not mean to tan it.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said. A formula that replaces an earlier report of a statement with the correct version.
An amount or measure
To shine or polish it
To tan it, which is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that רב חסדא still means 'if he intends to tan.' The new version is about the amount of oil. Using too much oil is forbidden even if the person has no plan to tan the leather.
steps.whatToRemember: Rolling on a leather mat after oiling the body is allowed only if the amount of oil can just polish the leather. If the amount is enough to tan it, it is forbidden, whatever the person intends.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
phrases.notes: The earlier version of the statement is dropped.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They only taught it for an amount enough to polish it,
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא's permission to roll on a leather mat.

phrases.english: but an amount enough to tan it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6 by rewording רב חסדא's statement from Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting how the statement was reported (rewording the מימרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא divided between intending to polish and intending to tan, which seemed obvious or impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא divided between an amount of oil that only polishes and an amount that tans. The tanning amount is forbidden even without intent.

steps.title: A child may not go out in a shoe that is too big, but may wear a cloak that is too big
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a small person may not go out in an oversized shoe, but may go out in an oversized garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A small person may not go out on שבת in a big shoe, but he may go out in a big cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about which shoes and clothes are safe to wear into a public area on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shoe that is too big may fall off, and the person might then pick it up and carry it in the public area. A cloak that is too big still stays on the body, so there is no such worry.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
A small person or child
A shoe
A cloak or robe

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea behind the whole ברייתא: we worry about anything that is likely to come off, because then it might be carried on שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A small person may not go out in a large shoe,
phrases.notes: It may fall off, and he may then carry it.

phrases.english: but he may go out in a large cloak.
phrases.notes: A cloak will not fall off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ברייתא, still on the topic of shoes on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shoe that is too big is forbidden to wear outside because it may fall off. A garment that is too big is allowed.

steps.title: A woman's torn shoe: not for going out, not to be used for חליצה at the start, but valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a woman may not go out in a shoe that is torn on top. Such a shoe should not be used for חליצה, but if it was used, the חליצה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a woman may not go out in a shoe torn on top, and she may not do חליצה with it. But if she did do חליצה with it, her חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another shoe that may not be worn outside on שבת, and adds a side point about using that shoe for חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People may laugh at her for the torn shoe, so she may take it off and carry it. For חליצה, a torn shoe is not a proper shoe to use at the start (לכתחילה). But it is still a shoe, so after the fact (בדיעבד) the חליצה counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Torn, usually meaning torn on top
The ceremony that frees a widow from יבום. She removes her brother-in-law's shoe.
She may do חליצה (literally, she may remove the shoe)
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: 'ולא תחלוץ בו' does not mean the חליצה fails. It only means you should not plan to use this shoe. If it was used, the חליצה still works.

phrases.english: And a woman may not go out in a torn shoe,
phrases.notes: She may be mocked, take it off, and carry it.

phrases.english: and she may not perform chalitza with it,
but if she performed chalitza, her chalitza is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another kind of shoe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A torn shoe may not be worn outside on שבת. For חליצה it should not be used at the start, but if used, the חליצה is valid.

steps.title: One may not go out in a new shoe
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that one may not go out on שבת in a new shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not go out in a new shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more forbidden case: wearing a new shoe outside on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new shoe may not fit well yet. The person may take it off and end up carrying it in the public area.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out, meaning into a public area on שבת
New

phrases.english: And one may not go out in a new shoe.
phrases.notes: It may not fit, so it may be taken off and carried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out on שבת in a new shoe is forbidden.

steps.title: The new-shoe rule applies to a woman's shoe
steps.stepSummary: A clarifying line limits the new-shoe rule to a woman's shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: About which shoe did they say this? About a woman's shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which new shoe the rule means and answers right away: a woman's shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women care a lot about how their shoes fit and look. So a woman is more likely to take off a new shoe that does not fit well. A man's new shoe is not part of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In which one? About which case?
They (the Sages) said

steps.whatToRemember: The whole ברייתא follows one idea: shoes or clothes likely to slip off or be taken off are forbidden outside on שבת, because the person may carry them. This includes a shoe too big for a child, a woman's torn shoe, and a woman's new shoe.

phrases.english: Regarding which shoe did they say this?
Regarding a woman's shoe.
phrases.notes: Women are particular about the fit of their shoes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule from Step 10 to a woman's shoe.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which new shoe does the rule mean?

steps.title: בר קפרא limits the new-shoe rule
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches that the ban on a woman wearing a new shoe applies only if she never wore it before שבת. If she wore it on ערב שבת, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: The rule against a new shoe applies only when she did not wear it outside even once while it was still day before שבת. But if she wore it outside on ערב שבת, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new source, from בר קפרא, narrows the rule we just learned about a woman not going out in a new shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with a new shoe is that it might not fit, and she will take it off and carry it. Once she has worn it on ערב שבת, she already knows whether it fits. So the worry goes away and the shoe is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this rule in the case of… (a phrase that limits a rule)
While it is still day, before שבת begins
The day before שבת, Friday

steps.whatToRemember: A new shoe is forbidden only if it was never tried out. Wearing it once on ערב שבת makes it allowed.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
They only taught (that a new shoe is forbidden)
where she did not go out in it even one time
while it was still day (before Shabbat)

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יָצְאָה בּוֹ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but if she went out in it on Shabbat eve, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: By then she already knows whether the shoe fits.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי בַּר קַפָּרָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further limits the new-shoe rule from steps 10 and 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new shoe is forbidden only if she did not wear it before שבת. If she wore it on ערב שבת, it is permitted.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about removing a shoe from a last
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says you may slide a shoe off a shoemaker's last on שבת. Another ברייתא says you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא taught: We may slide a shoe off a shoemaker's last. Another ברייתא taught: We may not slide it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to directly contradict each other. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A last (אימוס) is the wooden foot-shaped form a shoemaker uses to shape a shoe. Both sources speak about the same act on שבת, but one allows it and one forbids it. That is a clear contradiction the גמרא must solve.

keyTerms.meaning: One ברייתא taught… and another ברייתא taught… (a formula for contradicting sources)
We slide off or remove
A shoemaker's last, the foot-shaped form a shoe is built on

phrases.english: One baraita taught:
One may slide a shoe off a shoemaker's last,
and another baraita taught:
One may not slide it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: שׁוֹמְטִין מִנְעָל מֵעַל גַּבֵּי אֵימוּס, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: אֵין שׁוֹמְטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic about shoes: removing a shoe from a last on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about sliding a shoe off a last
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings for the same act.

steps.title: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא that forbids follows רבי אליעזר, and the ברייתא that permits follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a difficulty. This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and that ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות do not really contradict each other. They reflect a known argument about whether a shoe still on its last counts as a finished כלי. If it is not a finished כלי, it has no use and may not be moved. If it is a finished כלי, it may be handled.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty
This one… that one… (assigning each source to a different view)
The Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one (which forbids) is Rabbi Eliezer,
that one (which permits) is the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הָא — רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different Tanna (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect the argument between רבי אליעזר (forbids) and the רבנן (permit).

steps.title: The משנה about a shoe on a last
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה where רבי אליעזר rules that a shoe on a last is טהור and the חכמים rule it is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A shoe that is on a last: רבי אליעזר rules it טהור, and the חכמים rule it טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים really argue about a shoe on a last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says it is טהור because the shoe is not yet a finished כלי, so it cannot become טמא. That is why, by his view, it may not be moved on שבת. The חכמים say it is a finished כלי that can become טמא, so it may be handled on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Rules it pure, meaning it cannot become impure
Rule it able to become impure

steps.confusionAlert: "Pure" here does not mean the shoe is clean or better. It means the shoe is not yet a finished כלי, which is exactly why רבי אליעזר forbids moving it on שבת.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
A shoe that is on a last,
Rabbi Eliezer deems it pure (not yet a finished vessel),
and the Sages deem it able to become impure (a finished vessel).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the argument used in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about whether a shoe on a last is a finished כלי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about טומאה of a shoe on a last

steps.title: The רבנן's view fits well with רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the permitting view works well according to רבא, who allows moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור either to use the object itself or to use its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to רבא, who said: An object whose main use is for something forbidden may be moved, whether you need the object itself or you need its place. By his view, the ruling is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question. It first shows the permitting view fits רבא, and it is about to ask how it fits the other view, that of אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור, since it is used for shoemaking, which is forbidden on שבת. Sliding the shoe off moves the last a little, and that counts as needing the last's place. רבא permits that, so there is no problem for him. The phrase הניחא signals that a challenge against another view is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (according to one view); a setup for a challenge against another view
An object whose main use is for a forbidden activity
For the use of the object itself
For the use of the space it takes up
Fine; it works well

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the shoe-and-last case to the basic rules of מוקצה for a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור.

phrases.english: It works out well according to Rava, who said:
An object whose main use is for a forbidden activity,
whether for the use of the object itself,
or for the use of its place, is permitted (to move),
it is fine.
phrases.notes: Removing the shoe counts as needing the last's place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the permitting view from step 14 against the rules of moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permitting ברייתא (the רבנן) as it fits with views other than רבא's
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling fits רבא, who permits moving such an object for its place. The challenge against the other view is about to follow.

steps.title: How does the permitting ruling fit אביי?
steps.stepSummary: The permitting ברייתא fits רבא, but אביי only allows moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור for using the object itself, not for its place. So how can he allow taking a shoe off the last?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to אביי, who says that moving such an object is allowed when you need the object itself but forbidden when you need its place, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other אמורא, אביי, and asks how the permitting ברייתא could work according to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To slide the shoe off, you have to hold or shift the last. The last is a tool meant for forbidden work. אביי is stricter than רבא and does not allow moving such a tool just to get at something else. So the permitting ruling seems to clash with אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, the אמורא who is stricter here: a work-tool may be moved only to use the tool itself
For the need of the object itself, meaning using it for a permitted job
For the need of its place, meaning moving it because you want the spot it occupies
What can one say? A formula for a challenge that needs an answer

phrases.english: But according to Abaye, who said:
for the need of the object itself, it is permitted,
for the need of its place, it is forbidden.
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of Step 16: that step said the ruling fits רבא, and this step asks about אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permitting ברייתא, which according to Step 14 follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking off the shoe seems to require moving the last, a work-tool, and אביי does not allow that except to use the tool itself.

steps.title: The shoe is sitting loosely on the last
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a shoe that sits loosely on the last, so it slips off without moving the last.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A shoe that is loose on the last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for אביי by narrowing the case. The shoe is loose, so you can slide it off without moving the last at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the shoe is loose, the forbidden tool never gets moved. You only touch the shoe, which is fine. So אביי has no problem with the permitting ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a source to a specific case
Loose, meaning the shoe is not tightly stretched on the last

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here? With a loose one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the shoe was tight, so freeing it would require moving the last.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shoe is loose, so the last stays still and only the shoe is moved.

steps.title: רבי יהודה permits a loose shoe
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying that if the shoe is loose, it is permitted. This shows that 'loose' is a real case the תנאים discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, if it was loose, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה explicitly permits a loose shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 18 is not invented. A תנא really made a loose shoe the deciding factor. That makes it reasonable to read the permitting ברייתא as talking about a loose shoe.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא, introducing a supporting source
רבי יהודה, the תנא who permits when the shoe is loose

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it was loose, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 18 with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: That the permitting ruling is about a loose shoe
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה: אם היה רפוי מותר

steps.title: Only loose is allowed, which fits אביי well
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יהודה we learn that a tight shoe is forbidden. That fits אביי perfectly. This sets up the coming problem for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that it is loose, which implies that if it is not loose, no. This works well for אביי, who said that a tool meant for forbidden work may be moved for the object itself but not for its place. That is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי יהודה: a tight shoe is forbidden. It notes that this fits אביי, and it is setting up a challenge against רבא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה made 'loose' the reason for the היתר, so a tight shoe must be forbidden. With a tight shoe you would have to move the last, and אביי forbids moving a work-tool for anything other than using the tool itself. So for אביי the ruling makes complete sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason, used to point out exactly why something is allowed
But if not loose, no. An inference from the wording
It works out well (for one view). Usually followed by a challenge to the other view
An object whose main use is for work forbidden on שבת
Fine, it is well understood

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not ask anything yet. 'הניחא לאביי' only means 'this is fine for אביי'. The real attack, against רבא, comes in the next step.

phrases.english: The reason is that it is loose,
but if it is not loose, no.
This works well for Abaye, who said:
an object whose function is for a forbidden use,
for the need of the object itself, it is permitted,
for the need of its place, it is forbidden. That is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּרָפוּי, הָא לֹא רָפוּי — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי יהודה's ruling in Step 19 and sets up the challenge in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: Setup: the inference that a tight shoe is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Showing that the inference fits אביי prepares the contrast with רבא, which is the real attack.

steps.title: Why does רבא need the shoe to be loose?
steps.stepSummary: רבא allows moving a work-tool both for the object itself and for its place. So even a tight shoe should be allowed. Why does רבי יהודה say 'loose'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבא, who says it is allowed both for the object itself and for its place, why specifically a loose shoe? Even a tight one should be allowed too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. Under his lenient rule, a tight shoe should also be allowed, so רבי יהודה's limit to 'loose' makes no sense for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the problem was with אביי, and the 'loose' answer solved it. That same answer now creates a problem for רבא. His broad היתר would allow moving the last anyway, so 'loose' should not matter. Then רבי יהודה seems to disagree with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, the אמורא who is lenient here: a work-tool may be moved for itself or for its place
Why specifically this case? A challenge to a detail that seems unnecessary
Even if not loose, also (it should be allowed)

steps.whyThisMatters: The two sides have now flipped. The answer that rescued אביי puts רבא in trouble. This shows how one detail (loose versus tight) is tested against both opinions on מוקצה.

phrases.english: But according to Rava, who said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ, בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ מְקוֹמוֹ — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: whether for the need of the object itself or for the need of its place, it is permitted,
why specifically loose?
Even if not loose, it should also be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'הניחא... אלא...' pattern begun in Step 20 by attacking רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's broad היתר for moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה limits the heter to a loose shoe. Under רבא's rule even a tight shoe should be allowed, so רבי יהודה seems to argue with רבא.

steps.title: The 'loose' ruling belongs to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge against רבא. The 'loose' condition is רבי יהודה reporting the view of רבי אליעזר, not the view of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling is רבי יהודה speaking in the name of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It says the 'loose only' ruling is not the view of the חכמים. It is רבי יהודה reporting what רבי אליעזר holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a shoe still tight on the last is not a finished כלי yet, so for him it is מוקצה. Only a loose shoe counts as finished and may be moved. So the word 'loose' comes from רבי אליעזר's own reason. The חכמים, who permit taking the shoe off the last, can still permit even a tight shoe, just as רבא says.

keyTerms.meaning: in the name of (quoting someone)
the תנא who forbids taking a shoe off the last

steps.confusionAlert: The 'loose' condition here is not about כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור at all. For רבי אליעזר it is about whether the shoe counts as a finished item yet.

phrases.english: That [ruling] of Rabbi Yehuda
phrases.notes: Refers to the 'if it is loose, it is permitted' statement from Step 19

phrases.english: is in the name of Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: So it reflects רבי אליעזר's view, not the חכמים' view

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21 against רבא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution: the troublesome ruling belongs to a different תנא with a separate reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה's 'loose' ruling showed that the חכמים forbid a tight shoe, which would go against רבא
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'loose' condition is רבי אליעזר's view, based on whether the shoe is finished. The חכמים can permit even a tight shoe, which fits רבא

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה quoting רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves that the 'loose' ruling was said by רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר: if it was loose, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its answer. The ברייתא shows that the 'loose' ruling really is quoted from רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 brought this ruling without the attribution. This ברייתא gives the full source: רבי יהודה is passing along רבי אליעזר's opinion. That confirms the answer in Step 22 and closes the רבא and אביי discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: as was taught in a ברייתא
loose (the shoe slips off the last easily)
permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The shoe-on-the-last case does not disprove either אביי or רבא. The 'loose' condition comes from רבי אליעזר, who holds a tight shoe is not a finished item.

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a baraita]:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
If it was loose, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Loose means the shoe is already finished and no longer needs the last

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text that supports the answer in Step 22
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the 'loose' ruling is רבי אליעזר's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה says the ruling explicitly in the name of רבי אליעזר

steps.title: Hadran: closing פרק תולין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the twentieth פרק, תולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק תולין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of פרק תולין. It is a formula of parting and love for the learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no argument here. It simply shows that the topic of the last פרק is complete and a new פרק is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
the name of the פרק, taken from its first word

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] Tolin

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final answer in Step 23

steps.title: New משנה: moving a permitted thing that carries מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens. One may lift his son even while the child holds a stone. One may lift a basket with a stone inside. One may move תרומה טמאה together with pure תרומה or חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may pick up his son even though there is a stone in his hand. He may pick up a basket even though there is a stone inside it. And one may move ritually impure תרומה together with pure תרומה, and with חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new פרק. It lists cases where you may move something permitted even though a מוקצה item comes along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone and תרומה טמאה are מוקצה on their own, because they have no use on שבת. Still, the משנה allows moving them when they are attached to or mixed with something you are allowed to move. The coming גמרא will explain the limits of each case.

keyTerms.meaning: abbreviation for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה
a basket
impure תרומה, which no one may eat, so it is מוקצה
ordinary, non-sacred produce
one may move (carry from place to place)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the stone or the impure תרומה stops being מוקצה. It only says it may be moved along with the permitted item it comes with.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may take his son
even with the stone in his hand.
phrases.notes: The stone is מוקצה

phrases.english: And [one may take] a basket with the stone inside it.
And one may move impure teruma
together with the pure [teruma], and with non-sacred produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נוֹטֵל אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ וְהָאֶבֶן בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A permitted item may be moved even though a מוקצה item is held in it, placed in it, or mixed with it

steps.title: רבי יהודה: one may even lift out the תרומה from a nullified mixture
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה goes further. One may lift out the one portion of תרומה from a mixture of one part תרומה in a hundred parts חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: one may even lift out the מדומע in a mixture of one and a hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a further leniency to the משנה. On שבת, one may remove the required portion from a mixture where תרומה fell into a hundred times as much חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one part תרומה falls into a hundred parts חולין, it is nullified. Still, one portion must be taken out and given to a כהן before the rest may be eaten. That removal looks like 'fixing' food on שבת, yet רבי יהודה permits it. The implication is that the תנא קמא does not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: lift out (remove the תרומה portion)
a mixture of תרומה with חולין
one part in a hundred: the ratio where תרומה is nullified (one part תרומה in a total of 101)

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a new question beyond מוקצה: whether making a mixture usable counts as forbidden 'fixing' on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One may even lift out the [teruma from the] mixture
in [a ratio of] one and a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף מַעֲלִין אֶת הַמְדוּמָּע בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further leniency to the משנה's ruling about moving תרומה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, one may remove the required portion of תרומה from a mixture of one part in a hundred

steps.title: רבא's ruling on carrying a child with a purse around his neck
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that carrying out a living child with a purse on his neck makes one חייב for the purse. If the child is dead, one is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: רבא said: If someone carried out a living child with a purse hanging from his neck, he is חייב because of the purse. If the child was dead and a purse hung from his neck, he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section of the new פרק opens with a new ruling from רבא about carrying a child who has a purse on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gives two cases with opposite results. With a living child, the carrier is חייב, and only because of the purse. With a dead child, the carrier is פטור entirely. The next steps of the גמרא will examine why the living-child case works this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה; the marker that the analysis section begins
A baby or small child
A purse or pouch
Liable, here meaning he has done a forbidden act of carrying on שבת
Exempt from liability

steps.confusionAlert: Read רבא's words closely. He does not say the carrier is חייב for the child. He says he is חייב only because of the purse (משום כיס). The next step asks exactly why the child does not count.

phrases.english: Gemara: Rava said:
phrases.notes: Opens the גמרא section on the new משנה.

phrases.english: If one carried out a living baby
and a purse was hanging on his neck —
he is liable on account of the purse.
phrases.notes: The liability comes from the purse, not from the child.

phrases.english: If it was a dead baby
and a purse was hanging on his neck —
he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הוֹצִיא תִּינוֹק חַי וְכִיס תָּלוּי בְּצַוָּארוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא section on the new משנה, which dealt with lifting a child who is holding something.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Living child with a purse: the carrier is חייב for the purse. Dead child with a purse: the carrier is פטור.

steps.title: Why is he not also liable for carrying the child?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבא's first case again and asks why the carrier is not also חייב for carrying the child.
steps.simpleTranslation: A living child with a purse hanging from his neck: he is חייב because of the purse. But he should also be חייב because of the child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבא's first case and challenges it. Why is only the purse counted, and not the child?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a child from one domain to another looks like a normal act of carrying. So the carrier should be חייב for the child as well. רבא's wording, which counts only the purse, seems to ignore this.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him also be liable; a formula for asking why an extra liability is not counted

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹק חַי וְכִיס תָּלוּי לוֹ בְּצַוָּארוֹ —
phrases.english: A living baby with a purse hanging on his neck —
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes רבא again in order to question him.

phrases.english: he is liable on account of the purse:
But let him also be liable on account of the baby!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of רבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the carrier is חייב only because of the purse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The child is also carried from one domain to another, so he should count as a second act of carrying.

steps.title: רבא follows רבי נתן: a living being carries itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds like רבי נתן, who says that a living person carries himself. So carrying a living child does not count as carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא holds like רבי נתן, who said: a living being carries itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by linking רבא to the opinion of רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי נתן, a living person helps carry himself, so he is not treated as a load. That is why the carrier is not חייב for the child. Only the purse, which is a real object being carried, makes him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like רבי נתן
A living being carries itself, so it is not considered a load

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule חי נושא את עצמו explains why the child adds no liability. It also sets up the next question: does the child cancel out the purse too?

phrases.english: Rava holds like Rabbi Natan,
who said: a living being carries itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the child does not add liability.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the תנא whose view רבא follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Carrying a living child is a normal act of carrying, so it should make one חייב.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי נתן, a living being carries itself, so the child does not count as a load.

steps.title: Shouldn't the purse be secondary to the child, like a bed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges further. A משנה teaches that someone carrying a living person on a bed is פטור even for the bed. So the purse should also be secondary to the child.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the purse should be cancelled relative to the child! Didn't we learn in a משנה: someone who carries out a living person on a bed is פטור even for the bed, because the bed is secondary to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא again. It uses a משנה about a bed to argue that the purse should not make him חייב either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the living child does not count as a load, the משנה suggests that the things on him do not count either. In that משנה, the bed is treated as secondary to the person and gets no liability. The purse should then be secondary to the child, and the carrier should be fully פטור. The next step gives the גמרא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be cancelled, meaning treated as secondary and not counted on its own
Relative to, in comparison with
Didn't we learn in a משנה? A formula for bringing a משנה as a challenge
Secondary, an accessory to the main thing

phrases.english: But let the purse be cancelled relative to the baby,
didn't we learn in a mishna:
One who carries out a living person on a bed —
is exempt even for the bed,
because the bed is secondary to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיבְטַל כִּיס לְגַבֵּי תִּינוֹק, מִי לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer that a living being carries itself, and uses it to challenge the liability for the purse.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the carrier is חייב because of the purse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that a bed carrying a living person is secondary to him and gets no liability. The purse should likewise be secondary to the living child, so there should be no liability at all.

steps.title: A bed is secondary to a person, but a purse is not secondary to a child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the bed. A bed is considered secondary to the living person lying on it. A purse is not considered secondary to the child wearing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bed, compared to a living person, is treated as secondary to him. A purse, compared to a child, is not treated as secondary to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 30. It explains that a bed and a purse are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bed exists only to serve the person lying on it, so it is swept up in him and does not count by itself. A purse is a separate, valuable item with its own importance. It does not serve the child, so it keeps its own status and the carrier is חייב for it.

keyTerms.meaning: They treat it as secondary or unimportant (בטל) compared to the main thing
Bed
Purse or money pouch
A living person

phrases.english: A bed, relative to a living person, is considered secondary to him.
phrases.notes: The bed serves the person, so it is not counted as separate.

phrases.aramaic: כִּיס לְגַבֵּי תִּינוֹק — לָא מְבַטְּלִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: A purse, relative to a child, is not considered secondary to him.
phrases.notes: The purse has its own value and does not serve the child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה about the bed (Step 30).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the bed is secondary to the person, the purse should also be secondary to the child.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bed serves the person and is secondary to him. A purse is an independent item and is not secondary, so one is חייב for it.

steps.title: Why is one not liable for carrying the dead child?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבא's second ruling: carrying a dead child with a purse makes one פטור. It asks why the carrier is not at least חייב for carrying the dead child.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said that if the child is dead and a purse hangs on his neck, the carrier is פטור. But he should be חייב for carrying the child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבא's second case, the dead child. It asks why carrying a dead body is not a punishable act of carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of רבי נתן that 'a living person carries himself' only applies to a living child. A dead child cannot carry himself, so the dead body seems like an ordinary object being carried. The question is why the carrier is not חייב for the body.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead child
His neck
But let him be liable!

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats רבא's ruling from Step 27 on purpose. This is not a new ruling. It is quoted again so the גמרא can ask a new question about it.

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹק מֵת וְכִיס תָּלוּי לוֹ בְּצַוָּארוֹ — פָּטוּר:
phrases.english: If the child is dead and a purse is hanging on his neck, the carrier is exempt.
phrases.notes: Quoting רבא's second case from Step 27.

phrases.english: But let him be liable for carrying the child!
phrases.notes: A dead child cannot 'carry himself,' so why is there no liability?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the living-child case was settled, the גמרא moves to רבא's dead-child case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that carrying a dead child with a purse is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נתן's rule only exempts a living person. A dead child is like any object, so carrying him should make one חייב.

steps.title: רבא follows רבי שמעון: a labor not needed for its own sake is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds like רבי שמעון. Any מלאכה done not for its own purpose is פטור. Carrying out a corpse is that kind of מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא holds like רבי שמעון, who said: for any labor that is not needed for its own purpose, one is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why carrying the dead child is פטור. רבא follows רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person does not carry out a corpse because he wants the corpse in the new place. He only wants to remove it or bury it. This is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, so by רבי שמעון it is פטור. The purse is also פטור here, because in his grief the carrier treats it as unimportant next to the child.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view רבא follows here
A labor done not for the purpose it normally serves
One is exempt for it

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is a major principle across הלכות שבת. Carrying out a corpse is the classic example of it.

phrases.english: Rava holds like Rabbi Shimon,
who said:
any labor that is not needed for its own sake,
phrases.notes: Carrying out a corpse is done only to get rid of it.

phrases.english: one is exempt for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a specific opinion (אוקימתא לפי שיטה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Carrying a dead child should be a full act of carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: Carrying a corpse is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, which is פטור according to רבי שמעון, and רבא follows him.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: a father may lift his son holding a stone
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a person may lift his son even if the son is holding a stone. This suggests the stone is secondary to the child. So the purse on a living child should also be secondary, and רבא should not say one is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: A person may pick up his son even though there is a stone in his hand. (So the stone is secondary to the child. Why then is the purse not secondary?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling about the living child from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone is מוקצה and normally may not be moved on שבת. If the father may lift the child anyway, the stone seems to be treated as secondary to the child. Then a purse on a living child should also be secondary, which contradicts the גמרא's answer in Step 31.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
A person may take or lift his son
The stone in his hand (a מוקצה item)

phrases.english: We learned in a Mishnah:
A person may pick up his son
while the stone is in his hand?
phrases.notes: Implied question: so the stone is secondary to the child. The purse should be too.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נוֹטֵל אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ וְהָאֶבֶן בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the living-child case and challenges the distinction made in Step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling, and Step 31's claim, that a purse is not secondary to a child.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows moving a stone together with the child, which shows that an object held by a child is secondary to him. The purse should be the same.

steps.title: The school of רבי ינאי: the child longs for his father
steps.stepSummary: The משנה does not prove that the stone is secondary. It speaks of a child who badly longs for his father, so the father is allowed to lift him because the child might become sick otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: The משנה speaks of a child who has a strong longing for his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining the משנה as a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father is not allowed to lift the child because the stone is unimportant. He is allowed because the child longs for him so much that he could become ill if he is not picked up. This is a special exception, so it teaches nothing about the purse.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall or students of רבי ינאי
Strong longing; the child misses his father so much he could become ill
His father

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
It is speaking of a child who has
a longing for his father.
phrases.notes: He might become ill if not picked up, so it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּתִינוֹק שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּעֲגוּעִין עַל אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in Step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה permits lifting the child because the stone is secondary to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is permitted only because of the child's longing and the risk of illness. It does not show that the stone is secondary.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge to the school of רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge: if the reason is the child's longing, then something else should follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to question the answer of the school of רבי ינאי, and the full challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אי הכי' accept the previous answer for a moment and then test where it leads. The גמרא will show a problem that results from explaining the משנה this way.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the reason

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the answer given in Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation by the school of רבי ינאי (the child longs for his father).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is the child's longing, a problem follows. The details are completed on the next amud.
